en.title: Donald Iwerks, Disney Innovator and Co-Founder of Iwerks Entertainment, Dies at 96
en.summary: A titan of cinematic and immersive entertainment, Donald Iwerks, whose technical genius shaped visual storytelling for decades, has passed away at 96. His legacy extends from groundbreaking Disney projects to the pioneering large-format experiences of Iwerks Entertainment.
en.body:
The world of entertainment is mourning the loss of **Donald Iwerks**, a visionary engineer and filmmaker who passed away on July 9, 2020, at the age of 96. As the son of Disney Legend **Ub Iwerks**, the co-creator of Mickey Mouse, Donald inherited a legacy of creativity but forged his own path through unparalleled technical innovation. His career, spanning over six decades, left an indelible mark on both The Walt Disney Company and the broader landscape of immersive entertainment.

Iwerks joined The Walt Disney Company in 1950, initially as a laboratory technician. His talent and passion quickly saw him transfer to the fabled Studio Machine Shop, where he honed his skills and eventually took on the role of a camera technician. His early work contributed to iconic films such as **20,000 Leagues Under the Sea**, a project that foreshadowed his future impact on visual storytelling. Over a distinguished 36-year tenure at Disney, he was instrumental in developing and refining technologies that pushed the boundaries of what was possible in filmmaking and theme park attractions. His contributions were not limited to animation; he pioneered advancements in projection technology, 3D filmmaking, and large-format cinema, laying the groundwork for experiences that would captivate audiences for generations.

## A Legacy of Innovation

Beyond his foundational work at Disney, **Donald Iwerks** co-founded **Iwerks Entertainment** with former Disney executive Stan Kinsey. This venture specialized in creating large-format films and simulation rides, further cementing his reputation as a leader in immersive entertainment. His engineering prowess and creative vision were key to developing groundbreaking projection systems and screen technologies that offered audiences unparalleled visual experiences. These innovations were not just about spectacle; they were about telling stories in new, impactful ways, drawing viewers deeper into the narrative worlds they loved. His commitment to advancing cinematic technology ensured that audiences could experience films and attractions with a new level of depth and realism.

## Impact on Fans and the Industry

For fans of Disney, **Donald Iwerks** represents a crucial link to the studio's golden age of innovation, a period where technical wizardry directly fueled storytelling magic. His work on films and attractions provided the immersive quality that has become synonymous with the Disney brand. The large-format films and simulation rides developed by **Iwerks Entertainment** also opened up new avenues for theme parks and entertainment venues, offering experiences that were previously unimaginable. His passing is felt by cinephiles and theme park enthusiasts alike, as his technical achievements directly enhanced their enjoyment of beloved stories and thrilling adventures. He leaves behind a legacy that continues to influence how we experience visual media and entertainment.

## What's Next

While the details surrounding his passing have been shared, the full scope of his personal archives and any planned retrospectives or tributes are yet to be announced. However, the impact of his work is already visible in the continued evolution of large-format cinema and immersive attraction technologies worldwide.
